topStories.headline: NoPa Loses Its Only Full-Size Grocery Store as Lucky on Fulton Closes for Good
topStories.dek: The Lucky supermarket at 1750 Fulton Street shut its doors on September 11, displacing 48 employees and leaving NoPa without a large-format grocer.
topStories.body:
The Lucky supermarket at 1750 Fulton Street in the North of the Panhandle closed permanently on September 11, 2026, ending what had been one of NoPa's last remaining large-format grocery options. Parent company Save Mart Supermarkets cited sustained financial underperformance as the reason, telling employees and city regulators in a state WARN notice first filed in March that the store had lost money year over year despite a prior remodel. Save Mart senior director of communications Phil Keene wrote in the notice that the company had worked to enhance the location "but it has not shown the sales and profit needed to continue operations."

The closure affects 48 workers, though Save Mart said some may be eligible to transfer to other locations. NoPa Neighborhood Association President Ryan Booth called the news "disappointing and alarming." Supervisor Stephen Sherrill, who represents the area north of Fulton Street where the store sits, said in a statement he is committed to incentivizing new store openings and cracking down on retail theft, which the Chronicle reported had been a contributing factor alongside long-term financial losses.

Residents and University of San Francisco students who depended on Lucky — whose Fulton Street prices the Chronicle found to be among the lowest in the city — are now redirected to Trader Joe's, Arguello Market, Gus's Community Market, Whole Foods, Bi-Rite, and Target, all within roughly a mile. The larger fear expressed publicly by neighbors is what becomes of the building itself. The Fillmore Safeway, which also closed earlier in 2026, sat vacant for months afterward, and many worry the Fulton Street site could follow the same pattern.

Save Mart told SFist it is actively seeking a subtenant grocer to take over the lease. Separately, T&T Supermarket — Canada's largest Asian grocery chain — is still targeting a winter 2026 opening at City Center on Geary Boulevard at Masonic Avenue, roughly half a mile away. That opening, if it proceeds on schedule, would partially offset the grocery gap for NoPa and USF-area shoppers.

topStories.headline: 150 Hayes Conversion Moves Forward: Renderings Show Glass-and-Bronze Facade and 104 Apartments
topStories.dek: Design renderings released in August give the first detailed look at the planned office-to-apartment conversion at 150 Hayes Street, with the permit application listing a possible construction start as early as summer 2027.
topStories.body:
Design renderings for the planned office-to-housing conversion of 150 Hayes Street were made public in August 2026, offering the first detailed look at how architects Solomon Cordwell Buenz envision the rebuilt structure. The proposal by Emerald Fund and SDG calls for gutting the existing 1968-era interior, stripping the dated green facade, and replacing it with a glass-and-bronze exterior. A new seventh floor would push the building's height from 74 to 100 feet, bringing total floor area to roughly 158,250 square feet — including 128,300 square feet of housing.

The project would yield 104 apartments: 55 one-bedrooms, 42 two-bedrooms, and seven three-bedrooms, with parking for 88 vehicles and 108 bicycles. The permit application states construction could begin as early as summer 2027. Washington Capital Management is backing the project; Emerald Fund and SDG plan to acquire the property from the Academy of Art before the end of this year. The Academy used the building for office administration and student gatherings until the pandemic, after which it sat vacant.

Future residents at 150 Hayes are expected to share amenities such as a fitness center and co-working space with the adjacent 101 Polk Street development, which Emerald Fund previously built on the same former California State Automobile Association campus. The 150 Hayes conversion is one of only a handful of such projects moving forward anywhere in San Francisco, made possible by a low acquisition price combined with city fee waivers, transfer-tax cuts, and other policy changes the developers spent years lobbying for.

topStories.headline: HVNA Fall Meeting This Wednesday Brings D5 Supervisor and Board President to Hayes Valley
topStories.dek: The Hayes Valley Neighborhood Association community meeting on September 24 will feature District 5 Supervisor Bilal Mahmood and Board of Supervisors President Rafael Mandelman as guest speakers.
topStories.body:
The Hayes Valley Neighborhood Association is holding its fall community meeting on Wednesday, September 24, with two senior elected officials as guest speakers: District 5 Supervisor Bilal Mahmood and Board of Supervisors President Rafael Mandelman. The HVNA has confirmed the event on its website; coffee, beer, and wine will be served. Residents should check hayesvalleysf.org for the confirmed venue and start time before attending.

HVNA general meetings cover public safety, transportation and planning, neighborhood beautification, and small-business concerns — all of which have been active issues in Hayes Valley this year. The 400 block of Hayes Street remains under its Friday-and-Saturday car-free closure, the Saturday farmers' market has been running since June, the Hayes Valley Entertainment Zone launched in July, and the 150 Hayes office conversion has advanced to the permit stage. Having both the neighborhood's supervisor and the Board's presiding officer together at the same session gives residents an unusual direct channel to raise questions about any of these matters.

The meeting is free and open to all Hayes Valley residents.

moreNews.headline: T&T Supermarket Still Targeting Winter 2026 Opening Near NoPa at Geary and Masonic
moreNews.body: As NoPa absorbs the loss of Lucky on Fulton Street, a partial offset remains on the horizon: T&T Supermarket, Canada's largest Asian grocery chain, announced in March 2025 that it will open a roughly 50,000-square-foot store at San Francisco City Center — 2675 Geary Boulevard at Masonic Avenue, about half a mile from the now-closed Lucky. The company has targeted winter 2026 for the opening, though no updated date has been confirmed publicly as of this week. The space has been vacant since Best Buy closed in 2017, and would bring a full-service grocer with a bakery, sushi counter, and prepared foods to a location that also serves USF students and Kaiser Permanente workers nearby. T&T opened its first California store in San Jose earlier in 2026.

moreNews.headline: Hayes Valley Community Cleanup Runs Every Saturday Morning
moreNews.body: The Hayes Valley Neighborhood Association organizes a community cleanup every Saturday morning, giving residents a recurring opportunity to help maintain neighborhood streets and green spaces. Volunteers should visit hayesvalleysf.org for current meeting-point and timing details.
